FIELD NOTES / EDGE AI
a little more context.
DATA → MODEL → REAL WORLD

A good benchmark is a beginning.
Latency and false positives get a vote, too.

01what if the training data didn’t need a camera?Synthetic data · Unity · model evaluation+

I generated training imagery in Unity and trained PyTorch detection models to reduce dependence on manual annotation. The synthetic-only models reached near production-level seatbelt-detection performance.

Alongside that work, I benchmark TensorRT engines on Jetson Orin and build evaluation pipelines for precision, recall, and F1. The recurring question: how much accuracy can we keep within a real-time inference budget?

Earlier in the vision rabbit hole: corrosion detection ↓
02rust has levels. i taught a model four of them.NCAI · Computer Vision Intern · Summer 2024+

At the National Center for Artificial Intelligence, I built a YOLOv8 segmentation model for corrosion on offshore oil-rig structures. The dataset brought together 8,000+ annotated images from open sources, with four corrosion-severity levels.

The aim was to support maintenance inspections with automated segmentation and CUDA-accelerated inference.

YOLOv8RoboflowOpenImagesCUDA
Another vision experiment: reading number plates ↗
03yes, the mechanical part was real.Robots · an off-road buggy · a relief hexacopter+
FINAL YEAR · 2024–25

Four robots. One heavy problem.

In a team of four, I worked on a robot fleet for moving heavy loads, researching an 800 kg lifting target and refining designs with SolidWorks and COMSOL.

Design target, not a claimed tested payload.
CHASSIS LEAD · 2024

Less weight. More off-road.

Our buggy placed 4th among 16 teams in a national competition. Iterations on the chassis cut weight by 20% and costs by over 10%.

DESIGN LEAD · 2023

Six rotors. A very real budget.

I led design in a ten-person team building a hexacopter for emergency relief. Simulation helped reduce composite use and save over PKR 100,000. The project won Best Financial Planning among more than ten teams.

Apparently the budgeting theme follows me everywhere ↓
04before shipping it, try breaking it.CureMD · Software Quality Assurance Intern · Summer 2025+

At CureMD, I worked through test-case design, equivalence partitioning, boundary-value analysis, and flowcharting across the software development lifecycle. I also completed ISTQB CTFL 4.0 certification.

A useful interlude between building a thing and trusting that it behaves.
